trust_decision.summary: Whether an SSH server key presented on a hop is trusted is decided by a known_hosts lookup keyed on (host, port, key_type) in KnownHosts::validate, called per hop from ClientHandler::check_server_key with that hop's own options; anything that writes a known_hosts row must bind the key to the address of the hop that actually presented it.

landing_point.why: The summary names Web SSH and the store; the AutoAccept arm there calls KnownHosts::trust with the target's ssh_options.host/port for any HostKeyUnknown event, including one raised by a jump-host hop.

Web SSH session, Prompt mode: host/port shown to the user and stored in PendingHostKey were the target's, not the hop's
Web SSH create_session (target ssh_options captured and threaded into event loop at :142, :156)
PendingHostKey state carried between Prompt event and AcceptHostKey message
RCEvent::HostKeyUnknown public enum (lower-level API consumed by web-ssh, native ssh server, admin)
native SSH server session event handling (pattern update only)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: warpgate-protocol-ssh/src/client/mod.rs:196 and warpgate-protocol-ssh/src/client/mod.rs:759-761 (RCEvent::HostKeyUnknown carries no hop identity; the published fix adds host/port there so consumers stop substituting the target's address)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The admin key checker is an admin-only diagnostic that trusts via an explicit separate add_ssh_known_host call, so a solver fixing 'Web SSH' can argue it is a different feature and an admin-confirmed action.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Unknown keys must still be stored (AutoAccept) or offered for acceptance (Prompt) for each hop, bound to that hop's own address; AutoReject must still reject and Ignore must still pass. An over-broad fix that rejects unknown keys on jump hops, or stops storing on accept, breaks first-connect through a jump host.

O6_input_shapes: target behind one jump host (multi-hop chain; unknown key on jump hop)
verification mode Prompt followed by AcceptHostKey websocket message

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Admin 'check host key' returns the first host key received on the chain, which for a jump-host target is the outermost jump host's key; the admin UI then stores it via add_ssh_known_host under the target's host:port.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only diagnostic with an explicit human 'trust' click handled by a separate generic endpoint (warpgate-admin/src/api/known_hosts_list.rs:43-65) and a Svelte page (warpgate-web/src/admin/config/targets/ssh/KeyChecker.svelte:141-151); not 'Web SSH'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different crate (warpgate-admin) plus frontend; the fix only touched a pattern at :60

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Admin check-host-key replies true to HostKeyUnknown on whichever hop raised it, so the handler stores that hop's key regardless of Prompt/AutoReject mode.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Binding is correct (handler stores under the hop's own address at warpgate-protocol-ssh/src/client/handler.rs:107-112); it is a mode-policy issue, arguably intended for an admin tool.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Native SSH prompt path could store the accepted key itself using the session's target address (as Web SSH did), instead of leaving storage to the per-hop handler.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Web SSH manager did exactly this at warpgate-web-ssh/src/manager.rs:241-254; a maintainer mirroring that code into the native server would naturally use the target's options.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Known-keys listing/cleanup keyed only on the target's host:port, ignoring jump-host rows; a 'trust' button there could reuse the target address for a chain key.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Delete-target cleanup at warpgate-admin/src/api/targets.rs:307-317 already keys only on the target's own address.
